comment: Make sure to book parking ahead of time as there is limited space. Be prepared for lots of elevation changes, steep climbs and descents and uneven ground.
Def get there early. Beautiful views, some bears, well marked trails, would highly recommend
we started the trail at 4pm lol so we had to turn around at 6.8 km and i did not pause and unpause
awesome views def bring proper hiking shoes lots of rocks and roots on the trail
Watch out for the side trails I saw a bear I wish I got pictures but instead I just got out of there as fast as I could lol great hike! Challenging and worth it!
Blue trail was a little overgrown at times, poison ivy wasn't far away, and there are some hazardous sections that require good mobility. Lovely views.
Rough terrain, but very much worth the views. Wouldn‘t recommend bringing kids.
Trail well maintained. Start early if you want to be sure to have a parking spot. Many many people. Parking fee there (but free until May 15th). The trail is nicely done and easy to do.
Free parking until May 15th at the trailhead, great conditions
Amazing views!

Probably my favourite hiking spot! 
The views are beautiful and the forest is great. Just be aware… this is not a smooth terrain. It’s quite rocky. Highly recommend hiking boots and be prepared to take some steep steps up and down rocks. Well worth it!
Shaded hike. 15 degrees was perfect temp and no bugs.
It’s a nice hiking trail. But there are some part of the trail have rocks and roots. It is pretty challenge. It needs a good hiking shoes.

This is such a nice hike. If you’re used to hiking, it’s normal conditions. If you’re not used to hiking, you will likely find the trail rocky and lots of roots. It’s mainly flat ground, limited climbing rocks and they have the rocks set up like steps anyways. This is my favourite hike to do every year! My time and distance is because I go to the beach and back, you really only need two hours total to get to the viewpoint and back.
Runs along the coast line of Lion Head village. Full of beautiful look outs. Intermediate hike. Need good hiking shoes

It's a hard trail with lots of roots and rocks to navigate around. The trail to the lookout and back isn't too long, but if you go further, you'll get to a Rocky beach and more lookouts. After the lookout, some bits of the trail are along the cliff edge, though you don't feel it as much because there are shrubs around. We took the inland side trail back through the  forest, which was very pretty but hard to navigate because it was a bit overgrown. Overall, amazing experience! One of the best views from a trail in Ontario!
Look out point is incredible you feel as though you are on top of the world
Beautiful views and rugged trails love it. You hike near the edge of the escarpment so you have to be careful.
Amazing views! Just bring lots of water and bug spray.

Gets extremely crowded. Start of trail full of litter. Great views. Tons of poison ivy and bugs. Clearly marked and easy to navigate. You’ll lose service part way through so download the trail before you go.
Stop leaving your shit on the trail I picked up 8 water bottles.
Gorgeous birthday hike for Camryn!
One the best trails in Ontario , this hikes takes you through different landscapes such as cliffs , deep forest and pebble stone beach . It’s a 5hr trail and Watch out for rattlesnakes!

Little to no people in May, was able to park at the trailhead for $20. Took just under 3 hours, varied views along the water vs inland portion. Lots of trillium flowers in the inland area, which was nice to see!

Beautiful trail with several lookout points. Trail is very rocky and requires careful footing at some points. Continuing down the Bruce trail after the main lookout point brings you down to the bottom of the escarpment and then back up to complete the loop.
Park in town and walk to the trail entrance. Shuttle bus might run from June
Always an amazing hike. Almost no people. Loved having this beautiful space to ourselves. Like being on the ocean but without the palm trees!
Amazing
It takes a lot longer time than the app suggest
Awesome spring hike! Definitely wear good hiking boots as the trail is quite rocky and can be pretty slippery. Would do again!
Little slick due to the rain this morning but great this afternoon when the sun came out!
Amazing hike!

The reward when you get to Lion Head Lookout is amazing but the 3 km hike in is a mental challenge before a physical one. The terrain is very rocky with lots of exposed roots underfoot. It was pretty dry for us but the slightest moisture makes them slippery. Definitely hiking boots required.  There were no bugs and during the week there were no crowds. You are supposed to reserve a spot online beforehand but we got lucky and reserved and paid when we arrived.
Amazing trail, gorgeous views,  but be sure to wear proper footwear.
$30 parking is crazy. But great views and interesting trail, pebble beach is nice too, so worth it with a group.
Challenging but satisfying. Well marked and good upkeep. Few people on the side trails.
Beautiful views and a great 12k that was the right amount of challenging. Here for the long weekend and the crowds were real!

Great trail with lots of lookouts along the way. It was overcast when we started, but began pouring rain so we had to turn around rather than complete the Lion’s Head trail loop. 10/10 would recommend this hike, and will be back for a second try at this trail.
Once you get past the lookout it’s amazing. Before the lookout, it’s crowded and dirty with people littering everywhere.
Good hike with nice views.
Very rocky trail, a lot of ups and downs , difficult at times and hard on the ankles. The views were beautiful !!!
Great trail! Beautiful views all around. Beginning rocks can be tough if you have bad ankles, otherwise, a pretty reasonable trail. Great parking lot.
Part of Lion's head before phone shut off

I hiked about 15 km, it felt easy to the lookout and the view was breath-taking. From there it got harder as I had to watch my feet carefully walking on terrains - lots of ups and downs with rocks and roots. Well marked trail, very popular, many spots to take photos. There weren't many bugs.
Amazing hike

A pleasant hike with not too many bugs and rugged terrain that requires sturdy hiking shoes. While not as stunning as Bruce Peninsula National Park nearby, it's still a worthy visit. The $20 parking fee for a 4-hour slot requires online reservation in advance.
Great trail with nice viewpoints, no bugs or mud today but some sections are rocky and difficult. Loop side trails were not busy at all.

Started at 7:30am on long weekend Sunday and it was really quiet with only one other couple ahead of us. Fun trail that wasn’t too challenging. Muddy in several parts since it rained day before, rocks and roots were slippery (even dry areas) so definitely wear shoes with good traction. It’s just starting to get warm and there were a couple of slightly buggy areas but nothing too bad.
Favourite trail by far. The views are unreal and if you go early enough you’ll get a parking spot and won’t be very busy.
Last day parking for free
Nice lookouts!!
Great terrain. Nice stroll. Pretty views.
Little muddy in the first few KM, the trail guy who worked here said free parking after the 15th of October! Not too busy saw about 4 groups of people, beautiful views, very rocky, loved it
Well defined trail ...  terrain is roots and rocks ... beautiful scenery....

Excellent trail with exceptional views and lots of look outs to take them all in! Super busy from the parking lot until the look out but quieter for the rest of the trail. McKay's Harbour was super nice!

Fee needs to be paid online. Options include 4 hours or a full day.
Beautiful view and worth the hike. McKay Harbor was quiet and peaceful. Total time was a bit over 4 hours.

AMAZING, except for groups that were SUPER loud and people that left a bunch  of trash behind. Hate seeing that.
LOVED the trails mixed terrain and the views are absolutely gorgeous!
very rough terrain, have proper footwear, lots of water and food! don't forget your camera! And please clean up after yourself! lots of garbage on the trail
Awesome hike!! No bugs! Had to park down the street though, it's reserved parking at the main lot.
Great trail—dog loved it too. Be aware that the eastern shortcut noted on this trail is now closed, so you can only do the Inland Trail loop. Still worth every second.
Great trail

Decent trail, got attacked by 40-50 deer flies and had to sprint half a kilometre, at the beach. So no swimming. Super super busy. Parking is available along the street first come first serve or by reservation online at McCurdy.

The trail is wonderful, but hikers need to be aware of the numerous trails in the area, and pay attention to where each trail goes.  Please be aware that the McKay Harbour Overnight Rest Area has been closed by Ontario Parks and the Bruce Trail Conservancy (Peninsula section) due to abuse - long-term party camping, illegal fires and chopping down live trees.  It is regularly patrolled by Ontario Parks.  Fines will be issued.

The trail was extremely fun with lots to see. Parking at the trail head needs to be booked by appointment in advance prior to showing up. Parking in town is approximately a 15 minute walk, $15 for the day.
Beautiful
Part of the original trail is closed off so couldn’t do a complete loop. Expect to be a bit slower if it rained as there’s lots of mud and rocks.
absolutely stunning. the elevation can be intense at times but the scenery more than makes it worth it. favourite hike so far.
All trails should update this trail to show the recently revised route (see photo). Also note at the trail head parking spot you have to reserve to park. $20 for 4 hours or $30 for the  day.
Amazing views! Difficult terrain.
such a beautiful place. took 6 hours but enjoyed every but of it. highly recommended.

This is one of the most beautiful hikes in Ontario. The full loop is a must do for any avid hikers. We went from the main trail head to the beach and back (walking down the road to the school where we parked our car). As many have said the terrain is rocky so hiking boots are recommended. Read below for an important update as of June 12, 2021. 

The Lions Head Transit Authority is charging a whopping $35 dollars to park at the school down the road from the main parking lot (which fills up very fast) and no parking signs have been erected everywhere else. Pay and display with a 3hr max is available in select locations. The parking charge is for the day and includes a shuttle bus to the trail head)

As someone who has been coming here regularly for years I have no problem respecting and supporting the local community (even at a premium price) but $35 is outrageous. We spoke with a few others on the trail that we had met in Lions Head over the years who felt this would be their last time due to the cost. Understand this community couldn’t cope with the influx of tourists and we should all be willing to support them, even at a premium, however the cost seems excessive.
Very nice that it’s not paved hike.
Lovely hike! Beautiful day. Moss around. Not paved path.
Great trail, beautiful view.
Some slippery rocks but absolutely beautiful...
Alot more difficult then one would assume. Be safe and wear the correct gear

Uneven footing most of the trail. Lots of recent, visitor-created paths around the lookouts before and after Lion's Head. Plenty of great photo opps between lookouts (having the other party stand across another lookout)

Amazing views at the top. Trail has lots of roots, rocks, elevation, etc. Tons of side trails to explore.

very heavy traffic on weekends for the route towards the lookouts. significantly less so on the side trails. Could have dog off leash for the entire side trails.

Mixed trail, but mostly Canadian Shield rock. You really look down most of the time, to decide where to put your foot next. It would be in your best interest to use good hiking shoes/boots. I had planned to walk the whole loop, but decided it was too much for me (I'm 64). Too many hills for me, and without knowing what was in front of me, I decided to turn back. I also decided my route back would not be along the coast, but more inland, and it was a much easier trail. The views of the bay are beautiful, and there are more than one lookouts besides the main one, both before and after it. despite the difficulty I had, I'm glad I tried this trail. If I can get in better shape, I'll try it again.
Update: 
On Sept. 24 we tackled the trail again, this time starting at Cemetery Road and doing the loop counter-clockwise. Even though it rained heavily for about 2 hours, we completed the loop in 7 hrs 15 min. In my opinion, the loop is a bit easier this direction, especially the last 4 km.
